                          INTERVENOR MIKE AVERY'S
                         INITIAL POST-HEARING BRIEF
             (Opposing any route using Link K61 and supporting Route 894)

        Pursuant to the procedural schedule established in SOAH Order No. 6, Intervenor Mike
Avery files this Initial Post-Hearing Brief arguing against any route utilizing Link K61 and
advocating for the Applicants' "Best-Meets" Route 894.
        Of all 122 alternative routes proposed by the Applicants in the March 26,2026 Casey D.
Petty routing memorandum (Oncor-LCRA Exh. No. 5), the only routes containing Link K61 are
Routes 295, 296, 297 and 706 (the "K61 Routes"). The following table of key Commission routing
criteria taken from Oncor's latest revised constraints table (Oncor-LCRA Exh. No. 23) show how
these four K61 Routes compare with the Applicants' "Best Meets" Route 894:

          From the above table recapping key routing criteria, it is clear that the Applicants' "Best
Meets" Route 894 is superior to all of the four K61 Routes, especially since it scores the best on
the important criteria of shortest length, least cost, and fewest habitable structures. Route 894 also
has the fewest number of crossings of a U. S. or state highway, the second fewest number of stream
crossings, and no length within the visual foreground of a park or recreational area.

          A detailed demonstration was performed by Casey D. Petty, RE. and supported by the
hearing testimony of Brenda J. Perkins, RE. for the Applicants showing that Route 894 best meets
the Commission's routing criteria.           See Oncor-LCRA Exh. No. 5 (March 26, 2026 Routing
Memorandum at pgs. 5 - 6). Moreover, numerous Parties and their experts also support Route
894. See, e.g., the following expert testimony demonstrating that such route indeed "best meets"
all Commission routing criteria on the key routing criteria and on a wholistic basis:



Intervenor Mike Avery's Initial Post-Hearing Brief                                                Page 2
 •   Brian C. Andrews on behalf of Glenn and Ryan Hodge. J.T. Carothers Holdings LLC MCP 18
    LLC, and Schwertner Farms Inc. See Hodge-Schwertner Exh. No. 1.
•   Mark D. Anderson on behalf of Ben E. Keith Company and Jan Yates Boultinghouse Family
    Trust. See Yates Keith Alliance Exh. No. 5.
•   James W Daniel on behalf of Theon Ranches LP and Daniel and Kathryn Voss and D&M
    Davis Land & Cattle LP. See Theon-Voss Exh. No. 1.

        As described in the testimony of routing expert Mark D. Anderson, Route 894 is one ofthe
shorter routes; it is one of the lower cost routes; it has one of the lowest number of habitable
structures within 500 feet (which is tied for third lowest); and it is within the top third of routes
with lengths paralleling compatible ROW Yates Keith Alliance Exh. No. 5 at pg. 12, lines 12 -
19. Routing expert Brian C. Andrews points out that Route 894 is the lowest cost route with 85
or fewer habitable structures that does not use Links Jll or J26 (which two links pass within the
foreground visual zone of Colorado Bend State Park and Post Oak Ridge State Park). Hodge-
Schwertner Exh. No. 1 at pg. 8, lines 4 - 6. Mr. Andrews also notes that the only two routes with
fewer habitable structures than Route 894 (Routes 430 and 442) are more expensive than Route
894 by $45 million and $47 million respectively and also score poorly on length not parallel to all
compatible ROWs. Hodge-Schwertner Exh. No. 1 at pg. 8, lines 9 - 12. In his support for Route
894, routing expert James W Daniel points out that the length of Route 894 that is not parallel to
existing compatible ROWs is shorter than all but two of all the other routes and therefore it is
likely that there will be more property fragmentation by all other routes since they will cross
previously undisturbed property. Theon-Voss Exh. No. 1 at pg. 17, lines 3 - 6.

        In light of the clear superiority of Route 894 over the four K61 routes and all the other
proposed routes, the Commission should not hesitate to select Route 894 as the "best meets" routes
in this docket.
